requirements.quote: Concurrent requests on one key can each pass the check before any of them increments, so a key can exceed its quota slightly under load.
reserve atomically, either with a single conditional `UPDATE … SET used = used + 1 WHERE used < quota RETURNING` or with a row lock, so the check and the increment are one statement.
N concurrent requests against a key with K remaining calls succeed exactly K times. [type:integration]
A quota of 0 still blocks every call, and errors still fail closed. [type:unit]

deliverables.change: Rewrite consumeApiCall as one withWorkspace tx: SELECT api_key row FOR UPDATE, count this period's api.calls for the key, refuse at/over quota, else run incrementSql (from ../usage/meter.ts) and update last_used_at in the same tx. Keep ApiCallResult shape; add no new export.

New committed-pool test (pattern of usage/__tests__/concurrency.test.ts): key with quota K, N>K concurrent consumeApiCall with distinct request ids -> exactly K allowed, ledger count K; quota 0 blocks every concurrent call; a throwing db rejects (fail closed).

preserve.what: consumeApiCall signature and ApiCallResult shape ({allowed:true,used}|{allowed:false,used,quota}); sole caller apps/api/src/middleware/api-key.ts
Idempotent billing per request id and per-key (not per-workspace) quota, as tested in packages/core/src/api-keys/__tests__/api-keys.test.ts

validate.command: pnpm --filter @causedeck/core exec vitest run src/api-keys/__tests__/concurrency.test.ts src/api-keys/__tests__/api-keys.test.ts src/usage/__tests__/concurrency.test.ts src/__tests__/cross-tenant/services.test.ts

decisions.choice: Row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the api_key row) rather than a conditional UPDATE on a counter
decisions.justification: Quota is counted from the usage_event ledger (api-keys/index.ts:279-295); there is no used column, and the issue allows a row lock. Reuses exported incrementSql (usage/meter.ts:106) in the same tx.
